problem: The 1e-12 reproduction check of the Q0-replayed P3 prices is only achievable if P3b uses P3's root seed and a bit-identical eigh factor built with one BLAS thread. The spec states neither. Under the Randomness rule a literal P3b run would use root 2026100111 and 'no root is reused across items', so it would reproduce nothing. Building the eigh factor in a multithreaded parent gives a different valid 8x52 factor, and the check then fails at about 1e-6.
evidence: barrier_fast_classical.py seeds Sobol with default_rng([2026092333, dim, s]) and sets OPENBLAS/MKL/OMP/NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1 before importing numpy, so setup() runs in single-thread workers. attribution_summary.json gives two different T0 8x52 factor hashes: single-thread (Q0 replay) f980fbab...bbf and multithread 9de3a24b...b44. The 8x52 prices across valid factors differ by about 1e-6 relative (3.2816161 vs 3.2816194 vs 3.2817120). The replayed prices are stored at full precision in q0_provenance_replay.json (8x52 3.2816193580246855; 4x12 equal to archive 3.5188852273893136). With an identical factor and seed, only ULP-level differences remain (other GEMM, ndtri or chunking), about 1e-15 relative, so 1e-12 is then achievable.
fix: Replace the Validation bullet with: 'Validation (port check, run before any canonical-basis run): P3b in preint/knock-out mode with P3's settings: root seed 2026092333 (a deliberate, disclosed reuse of the P3 root for this check only), 32 scrambles, Sobol stream [2026092333, dim, s], CHUNK 2^12, n = 2^17. L is built by P3 setup() in each worker process with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = MKL_NUM_THREADS = OMP_NUM_THREADS = 1 set before numpy is imported. Assert sha256(L) for 8x52 equals f980fbabce8234cbf92aa888b02f15004ea53a55e6f456de41980be56b2ebbbf (T0 single-thread, attribution_summary.json). Pass: |price - replayed| / replayed <= 1e-12 for both cases (replayed values from q0_provenance_replay.json / the archive for 4x12), and per-n sd within 1e-9 relative. A hash mismatch is reported as a setup failure, not a port failure.' In section 0, replace 'between numpy 1.26 and 2.0' with 'between LAPACK builds and thread counts (numpy 1.26.4/MKL versus 2.0.2/OpenBLAS, and 1 versus many threads)'.

section: C3 Ref A and agreement-test resolution
problem: Ref A's target (99% half-width <= $2.5e-5, n capped at 2^22) is unreachable by about 7-21x. The C3 resolution goal of eps/10 = $1e-4 is therefore unreachable because of Ref A, not plain MC. The spec attributes any shortfall to plain MC only. The pilot rule ('n chosen from a 2^14 pilot') also needs a rate to extrapolate, and none is fixed.
evidence: Time-ordered OSS (P2, barrier_oss_pilot.json) has r = 0.479, sd(2^15) = 0.01638 at 8x52 and r = 0.571, sd(2^15) = 0.00886 at 4x12. Extrapolated to 2^22 with 64 scrambles (t_.995,63 = 2.656): hw99 is about 5.3e-4 (8x52) and 1.8-2.2e-4 (4x12). Reaching 2.5e-5 would need about 2^31 (8x52) and 2^27 (4x12) points per scramble. Compute is not the constraint: 64 x 2^22 points cost about 7.5 process-hours (28 min wall) at 8x52 and about 1.4 process-hours (5 min) at 4x12, assuming about 100 and 19 us/point with contention. Resolution hw99(A) + hw99(B) is then about 6-8.5e-4 (0.6-0.85 eps) at 8x52 and 2.3-3.5e-4 at 4x12, depending on Ref B (separate finding).
fix: Replace the Ref A sentence 'n per scramble is chosen from a 2^14 pilot ... capped at 2^22' with: 'n = 2^22 per scramble, fixed now (the pilot-based target of $2.5e-5 is not reachable: from P2's rates the expected hw99 is about 5e-4 at 8x52 and about 2e-4 at 4x12).' Replace 'If plain MC cannot reach it within budget' with 'Neither reference is expected to reach it; the expected resolution is about $6-9e-4 (8x52) and $2-4e-4 (4x12); the achieved resolution is reported as a limitation.' In the C4 bullet, replace 'The C4 reference value is Ref A if the agreement test passes' with 'If the agreement test passes, the C4 reference is the inverse-variance-weighted mean of Ref A and Ref B (both independent of P3), with its own hw99; otherwise C4 is run against each.'

section: C3 Ref B budget and GPU option
problem: '12 CPU-hours per case, or 2 GPU-hours' is ambiguous: process-hours and wall-clock hours of the 16-process pool differ by 16x in paths. The two options are not equivalent: the GPU gives about 3.6x better 8x52 resolution than 12 process-hours. The GPU path cannot use the stated 'PCG64 streams' (numba.cuda provides xoroshiro128p). 'Validates its kernel against the CPU at 10^6 paths' cannot be an exact check with different RNGs, and at 10^6 paths it is only a ±$0.013 statistical check. Two GPU-hours per case also consumes the plan's entire GPU budget (plan section 7: ≤ 4 GPU-hours). Which option is used depends on C6 progress, the first item on the cut list.
evidence: Measured in the T0 venv: 16 concurrent numba plain-MC processes give 5.26e6 paths/s (4x12) and 6.68e5 paths/s (8x52); a single process gives 2.32 and 17.1 us/path. A numba.cuda float64 xoroshiro128p plain kernel on the RTX 4060 Laptop gives 1.35e7 (4x12) and 3.22e6 (8x52) paths/s. Pointwise plain sigma is 5.66 / 5.19 (P1). hw99 for 4x12 / 8x52: 12 process-hours gives 1.2e-4 / 3.2e-4; 6 wall-h x 16 processes gives 4.3e-5 / 1.1e-4; 12 wall-h x 16 gives 3.1e-5 / 7.9e-5; 2 GPU-hours gives 4.7e-5 / 8.8e-5. Plan C3: 'budget 40–60 CPU-hours, run overnight on Days 2–4'.
fix: Replace the Ref B bullet with: 'Ref B: plain iid MC (exact-date one-factor time stepping, plain knock-out payoff) in numba on 16 CPU worker processes, each with its own PCG64 stream from SeedSequence [2026100131, case_index, 2, worker]. Budget, fixed now: 6 wall-clock hours per case on the 16-process pool (96 process-hours per case, 12 wall-clock hours for both cases, one overnight slot). The plan's "CPU-hours" is read as wall-clock machine hours, and this reading is disclosed. Expected hw99: about 4e-5 (4x12) and 1.1e-4 (8x52). The run stops at the budget, whatever the running difference. The GPU is not used for Ref B.' Then delete '(or on the GPU once C6 validates ...)' and ', or 2 GPU-hours'.

section: C6 host Sobol pipeline (primary GPU T_C)
problem: Two things are unspecified: how many host processes generate the Sobol points, and which stages run on the host ('as in P3' includes scipy ndtri and the PCA GEMM). Either choice can be tuned after the GPU timings are seen, and the host part dominates the end-to-end time. If the host keeps P3's Sobol+ndtri+GEMM, Amdahl's law caps the end-to-end GPU factor at about 2 even with an infinitely fast kernel. With a single feeder process the GPU would be about 5x slower than the 16-worker CPU.
evidence: P3 per-point components, single process in T0 (8x52): scipy Sobol 2.8 us, scipy ndtri 31.6 us, BLAS GEMM 20.6 us, numba estimand 50.7 us (host share 52%). For 4x12: 0.5 / 6.7 / 2.0 / 18.7 us. The CPU 16-worker P3 runs at about 1/(1.6-2.1e-4 s) x 16 = 0.8-1.0e5 points/s (archive and Q0 logs). One host feeder doing Sobol+ndtri+GEMM manages about 1.8e4 points/s. GPU float64 is feasible: compute capability 8.9 and a measured float64 exp+erfc throughput of 1.06e9 pairs/s. That bounds the 8x52 preint kernel at about 2.6e5 points/s (about 8,000 transcendental calls per point), so the kernel-only factor is likely 1-3. Host-to-device traffic of 3.3 KB per point is not limiting. scipy Sobol supports up to 21,201 dimensions.
fix: Replace 'Sobol points are generated on the host, as in P3, and transferred' with: 'Scrambled Sobol uniforms are generated on the host with scipy (same seeds as the CPU run) by exactly 4 feeder processes, in chunks of 2^16 points, and transferred as float64. Inverse normal (CUDA normcdfinv), the PCA product and the estimand run on the device. The feeder count and chunk size are fixed now and are not tuned after timing.' Add: 'Sensitivities (classical-favourable, labelled): kernel-only time; 8 feeders. Quantum-favourable sensitivity: host ndtri+GEMM as in P3.'

problem: P3b's pipeline is not pinned. T_C enters D_max linearly, and implementation choices move per-point time by 30-50%: scipy ndtri versus a numba inverse normal, BLAS GEMM versus numba, CHUNK size, and recomputing setup() per scramble. Under symmetric pre-specification these choices could otherwise be revisited after seeing the C2 timings.
evidence: Single-process T0 profile of P3 at 8x52: ndtri is 31.6 of 105.7 us/point (30%), and GEMM is 20.6 us (19%). P3 calls setup() (eigh of the 416x416 Kronecker covariance) in every scramble task (median 0.45 s, archive). ERRATA E5 shows that per-point accounting choices already moved the 4x12 T_C by 2.6x (5.9 s to 2.25 s).
fix: Add to C1: 'P3b keeps P3's per-chunk pipeline as the primary timing convention (quantum-favourable): scipy Sobol.random(CHUNK = 2^12) -> scipy.special.ndtri(clip(u, 1e-15, 1-1e-15)) -> single-thread BLAS GEMM (BLAS threads set to 1 before numpy import) -> numba estimand (cache=True, fastmath=False). The basis is built once per worker process. A numba inverse normal or a fused numba GEMM may be timed only as a labelled classical-favourable sensitivity.'

problem: 'Run 20 replications at n(eps)' leaves three outcome-relevant choices open. (1) Rounding: n(eps) is real-valued and is not a power of 2, while scrambled-Sobol balance and the fitted rates hold at powers of 2. (2) The pass criterion for the 'achieved 99% t half-width': by construction about 45% of replications will exceed 0.45 eps even when the model is exact. (3) The primary T_C when n(eps) > 2^21 or when the achieved accuracy misses.
evidence: From the archived fits (t_.995,15 = 2.947), n($0.001) for preint is 1.25e5 = 2^16.9 (8x52) and 9.9e4 = 2^16.6 (4x12). Plain RQMC knock-out (P1 fit) gives 2^21.5-2^21.6, which is above 2^21, so it is not confirmed. With 16 scrambles the sample sd exceeds the true sd with probability P(chi2_15 > 15) = 0.45. barrier_decision.py uses real-valued n, while P1 budgets() rounds up to a power of 2, so both conventions have precedent. Rounding to 2^17 adds 5% (8x52) and 32% (4x12) to the measured T_C, which enters D_max linearly.
fix: Replace the Measured confirmation bullet with: 'For eps in {$0.01, $0.001} and each (case, method) with n(eps) <= 2^21: run 20 replications of the 16-scramble estimator at n_run = 2^ceil(log2 n(eps)) (quantum-favourable; it keeps Sobol balance). Scrambles are fresh, from seed key [2026100121, case_index, 3, eps_index, replication, s]. Record each wall time (all-16 maximum) and achieved 99% t half-width. Primary T_C = median wall time over replications. Report the fraction of replications with half-width <= 0.45 eps, and the half-width computed from the pooled 320 scrambles. If the pooled half-width exceeds 0.45 eps, the primary T_C is the measured median wall time x (pooled hw / 0.45 eps)^(1/r). Where n(eps) > 2^21, the primary T_C is the C1/C2 model value, marked extrapolated.'

problem: C7 (2^18 fallback for 16x52) and C8 (prefixes only to 2^17) cannot use the primary window m in [10, 19], and no replacement window is fixed. The window then becomes a post hoc choice that sets r, n(eps) and the stop-rule ratio. The bootstrap and extrapolation flags are also undefined for these runs.
evidence: Spec C1: 'Primary window m in [10, 19]'. C7: 'to 2^18 for 16x52 if a scramble takes more than 10 minutes'. C8: 'C1 (preint, 32 scrambles, to 2^17)'. Historical P3 used n >= 2^9 up to 2^17. Measured 16x52 single-process cost is 253 us/point (about 430 us with 16-worker contention), so a 2^19 scramble takes about 3.8 min and the 10-minute trigger is not expected to fire.
fix: Add to C1: 'For runs whose top prefix is 2^M with M < 19, the primary window is m in [10, M] and the sensitivity windows are [8, M] and [max(10, M-5), M]. The same bootstrap (B = 4000, seed 2026100112 with the case index appended) is used. n(eps) > 2^M is marked extrapolated.' Add to C7: 'The 2^18 fallback is decided from the wall time of the first completed scramble of the 16x52 H = 140 case, before any rate is computed, and applies to all three 16x52 cases.'

section: C7 / C8 stop-rule inputs (sigma_Q and T_C convention)
problem: The 'unchanged stop rule' needs the plain-payoff pointwise sigma_Q for each new case, and no step of C7 or C8 estimates it: preint RQMC does not give it, and H, sigma, rho, K and T all change it. It is also unstated which T_C convention feeds the rule: the historical per-scramble-median model, the new all-16 wall-time model, or a measured confirmation (C7 and C8 run no confirmation). These choices move D_max and can be picked after seeing the ratios.
evidence: barrier_decision.py takes sig_plain = P1 pointwise_std['barrier'] (2^14 iid normals, seed [2026092231, 7, dim]) and computes classical_seconds = setup + n x (t_full - setup)/2^m_max from per-scramble medians. barrier_oracle_depth.build hard-codes SIGMA, CORR, S0, RATE, T, K, H as module constants. The scored depth depends only on (na, nt), because the favourable table charges by op type. The plain MC kernel costs 2.3-36 us/path single-core, so 2^16 iid paths cost under 3 s per case.
fix: Add to C7 and C8: 'sigma_Q (plain knock-out payoff) per case from 2^16 iid exact-date paths, PCG64 SeedSequence [root, case_index, 7]; the preint sigma is reported as a sensitivity. The stop rule uses the historical convention exactly: T_C = median setup + n(eps) x warm per-point time, from the per-scramble median elapsed times of the C2 warm repeat(s), with n(eps) from the case's primary-window fit. The all-16 wall-time model is reported as a sensitivity. No measured confirmation is run for C7 or C8.'

section: Outputs and gates / schedule (cut list, run exclusivity)
problem: The gate accepts any item 'reported as not done with the reason', with no cut order or trigger fixed in advance. An item can therefore be dropped after partial results are seen, for example C8 after an unfavourable case. Nothing requires timing-bearing runs to own the machine, yet the overnight Ref B, Ref A and C4 jobs would saturate the same 16 workers during C2, C5, C7 or C8 timing. Contention already moves per-point time by about 30%.
evidence: Plan section 4 cut list: 1. C6 GPU -> carry g; 2. Q6; 3. C8 -> not done; 4. C5 -> weaken C2 wording. The 8x52 P3 per-point time was 206 us in the archive run and about 161 us in the Q0 replay on the same laptop, against 106 us for a single uncontended process. Estimated exclusive wall time from archived and measured per-point costs: C1 15 min per basis (60 min for 4 rotations; 22 min if the rotations cover only the knock-out); C2 17 min of repeats plus 12 min of confirmation; Ref A 33 min; C4 28 min with nested prefixes (53 min with independent n levels); C5 25 min; C7 74 min; C8 45 min; Q4 under 20 min single-process. Total about 5.2 h of machine time plus Ref B (12 h overnight at the proposed budget). Development work, not compute, is the bottleneck: P3b plus basis about 0.5 day, OSS/Ref B about 0.5 day, OSS-BB about 0.5 day, the CUDA port about 1 day, and the Q4 reference about 0.5 day.
fix: Add a section 'Schedule, exclusivity and cuts (fixed now)': (a) Timing-bearing runs (C2, C5 timing, C6, and the C2 repeats inside C7 and C8) run with no other Stage C job active. Ref A, Ref B, C4 and the C1 rotations run only in other slots. Each JSON records the load average and the concurrent-job list. (b) Order: Day 1: P3b, canonical basis and tests, C1 validation, C1 canonical, C2; overnight: Ref A, Ref B (2 x 6 h), C4. Day 2: C1 rotations, C5, C7, Q4. Day 3: C8, then C6. (c) If the work slips, cuts are applied only in the plan's order (C6 -> carry g ∈ {1,10,100}; C8 -> not done; C5 -> C2 worded 'for the two smoothers tried'). A cut is decided at the start of a day, before that item has started, from elapsed time only. An item that has started is completed and reported. Pre-declared compute trims before any cut: rotation sensitivity for the knock-out only (saves about 40 min); C4 with nested prefixes.'

problem: The key [root, dim, scramble] has no case index, so cases with the same dimension share identical Sobol scrambles. This affects C7 (4x12 and 8x52 at H = 120 and 160) and C8, where the four cases in each stratum share na x nt, so their errors are correlated across cases. The key also has no purpose or replication index for C2 repeats, the 20 confirmation replications, C4's 16,000 scrambles or the Ref B iid streams. The rotation key uses 'case', which is not an integer, and the random-rotation algorithm is not stated, so the exact replay tier cannot regenerate the rotations.
evidence: P1, P2 and P3 all use default_rng([ROOT, dim, s]). C8 strata fix (na, nt), so within a stratum dim is constant for j = 0..3. Spec: 'PCG64 SeedSequence [2026100101, case, rotation]'.
fix: Replace the Randomness bullet's key with: 'SeedSequence [root, case_index, purpose, replication, scramble]. case_index comes from a table in the runner, committed with this file (development 4x12 = 0, 8x52 = 1; C7 cases 2-8; C8 cases 100 + 4s + j). purpose: 0 rate, 1 timing, 2 iid reference, 3 confirmation, 7 sigma. dim is recorded but not used as a key.' Replace the rotation sentence with: 'Rotation q (q = 1..4) inside each exactly repeated eigenspace of dimension d is Q·diag(sign(diag R)) from numpy QR of a d x d standard-normal matrix drawn from SeedSequence [2026100101, case_index, q], eigenspaces taken in canonical order.'

problem: The spec never requires streamed chunks. On this 15.4 GB machine, unchunked draws are infeasible: a single Ref A call at 2^22 x 416 is 14 GB, and C7 16x52 at 2^19 per worker is 3.5 GB x 16 workers. scipy also warns, and loses balance, when n is not a power of 2.
evidence: Measured total RAM is 15.4 GB. scipy 1.13.1 Sobol has MAXDIM 21,201 and default bits = 30, so 832 dimensions and 2^22 points are within limits. Scramble initialisation costs 0.010 s (48 dims), 0.058 s (416) and 0.123 s (832) per scramble, which is negligible even for C4's 16,000 scrambles per case (about 1 min wall). P1, P2 and P3 all stream CHUNK = 2^12.
fix: Add to section 0: 'All runners stream Sobol points in chunks of 2^12 (2^16 for GPU feeders) through Sobol.random, with no fast_forward, and never materialise more than one chunk per worker (about 1.3 GB peak for 16 workers at 832 dimensions). Every run size and prefix is a power of 2.'

section: Q4 draw counts and IR pin
problem: The fallback ('if B8x52 IR evaluation would exceed 8 CPU-hours, it uses 2,000 + 2,000 draws') contradicts the plan's '≥ 10^4 draws' pass criterion, and it is moot because evaluation is fast. The spec also does not pin which Stage A IR file is evaluated (original or optimized target, with hash).
evidence: Measured with ir.evaluate in the T0 venv: B8x52 takes 0.072 s/draw (original_target.json, 42,486 nodes) and 0.073 s/draw (target.json, 41,654 nodes). B4x12 takes 0.008-0.009 s/draw (about 5,100 nodes; 60 inputs; B8x52 has 468 inputs). 10^4 B8x52 draws take about 12 min in one process, under 1 min on 16 processes. 10^7 float64 knock-out paths take about 3 min single-core at 8x52 (17 us/path). Plan Q4: '≥ 10^4 draws, stratified near the barrier'.
fix: Delete the 8-CPU-hour fallback sentence. Add: 'The IR evaluated is results/frontier_completion_20260927/stage_a/<case>/target.json, with its sha256 from artifact_hashes.json checked before use. Draws are split over 16 processes; expected wall time is under 5 minutes.'

section: Q4 independent reference and barrier-bias bound
problem: 'Box–Muller from the same uniforms, GBM ...' does not fix the IR's input law. A careful independent implementation (for example P3's PCA path construction) would therefore produce spurious 'errors'. The 'upper 99% bound' from 10^7 paths has no stated method. With δ_fp of order 1e-9 the expected event count is about 0, so a CLT bound would be a degenerate 0.
evidence: finance.normals_graph maps 32-bit inputs to midpoints u = raw/2^32 + 2^-33 and pairs inputs (2j, 2j+1) as r·cos 2πv and r·cos 2π(v+0.75) = r·sin 2πv, with r = sqrt(-2 ln u). barrier_oracle_depth.build uses nt(na+1) normals: index j(na+1) is the common factor (σ√(ρ dt)) and j(na+1)+1+i the idiosyncratic factor of asset i (σ√((1-ρ)dt)). The drift is (r - σ²/2)dt, prefix-summed from ln S0, clipped to [ln 2^-16, ln 4096], with strict comparison max basket < H. Plan Q4 states the bound as jump x P(|max basket - H| ≤ δ_fp). (A-K)+ ≤ H-K on the surviving set.
fix: Add to Q4: 'The NumPy reference uses the IR's input law: u_i = (raw_i + 1/2)/2^32; normals in pairs (2j, 2j+1) as r cos 2πv, r sin 2πv; per date j, normal j(na+1) is the common factor and j(na+1)+1+i the idiosyncratic factor of asset i; no spot clip (clip events are counted separately).' Replace the bound sentence with: 'Bound = e^(-rT)(H-K) x the one-sided 99% Clopper–Pearson upper limit of P(|max_j basket_j - H| ≤ δ_fp), from 10^7 iid float64 paths (PCG64 [2026100191, case_index, 7]). With zero events this is about $1.8e-5. δ_fp is the maximum observed basket error and is labelled empirical, not certified.'

section: C5 decision statistic and OSS-BB dimension order
problem: 'If no method reaches r ≥ 0.9 at 8x52' does not say which r decides it: the point estimate in the primary window, the bootstrap upper or lower percentile, the canonical basis or any rotation, C1 or the confirmation. The claim C2 wording ('dropped or reversed') hangs on that choice. For OSS-BB, the Sobol order across the na-1 bridged PCs (level-major or PC-major) is open, and it changes the rate. 'Unbiasedness is checked against Ref A' has no criterion.
evidence: Spec C5 text. C1 already defines a primary window [10, 19], a bootstrap and rotations, but C5 does not bind to them. DECISION section 6's original rule is 'any classical finalist reaches r ≥ 0.9 on all development cases'.
fix: Replace the C5 claim sentence with: 'A method reaches the threshold if its primary-window (m in [10,19]) point estimate of r under the canonical basis is ≥ 0.9 at 8x52; the bootstrap 95% interval and the rotation spread are reported but do not decide.' Add: 'OSS-BB Sobol order: dims 1..nt are the PC1 increments in date order; then bridge levels coarsest first, with the na-1 PCs interleaved inside each level (level-major, PC 2 first). Unbiasedness passes if |OSS-BB - Ref A| ≤ hw99(OSS-BB) + hw99(Ref A) at 2^19 x 32 scrambles.'

section: C3 Ref A construction versus plan
problem: The plan's C3 reference is 'numba bridge-ordered one-step survival'. The spec's Ref A is P2's time-ordered OSS, and bridge ordering moves to C5 (OSS-BB). This deviation from the plan is not disclosed. Keeping time-ordered OSS for Ref A is defensible, because it keeps C3 independent of C5, which is on the cut list. The cost is resolution: P2's time-ordered rate at 8x52 is 0.479.
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Track C, C3: 'numba bridge-ordered one-step survival, and numba plain iid MC on 16 processes'. Spec C3 Ref A: 'P2's basket OSS estimator ... ported to numba'. barrier_oss_pilot.py advances dates sequentially (time-ordered).
fix: Add to C3: 'Deviation from the plan, stated now: Ref A is the time-ordered OSS of P2 (not bridge-ordered), so that the reference does not depend on C5, which may be cut. The bridge-ordered variant is C5's OSS-BB and is compared with Ref A there.'

problem: The spec takes 'the quantum k from the explicit bounded estimator schedule already archived (estimator_bounded.json)' without saying how to turn that schedule into a knock-out k. The archived schedule is specific to the compound model, and the plan says it is 'not transferable as a constant'.
evidence: estimator_bounded.json rows are for models C4/H8 (for example span 256, error 0.00203, 7,864,305 controlled Grover calls, 99.7% certified). Plan section 2 assets table: 'Built for the compound residual estimand; not transferable as a constant'. The empirical-Bernstein side needs the knock-out range (H-K)e^(-rT) = $38.8 and sigma, which are defined.
fix: Replace the C4 sensitivity's quantum side with: 'k_explicit = (controlled Grover calls) x (certified error) / (span) from estimator_bounded.json, applied to the knock-out range (H-K)e^(-rT) at failure probability 0.01. It is labelled as transferred from the compound estimand (plan section 2 caveat) and is not a knock-out-specific schedule.'

problem: The plain-MC anchor's path construction is not fixed. One-factor time stepping and the PCA GEMM path differ several-fold in throughput at 8x52, so the anchor could be picked after the fact. The float64 feasibility claims hold (see evidence); stating them prevents a later 'float64 too slow' substitution.
evidence: T0 measurements on the RTX 4060 Laptop (CC 8.9, 24 SMs), numba-cuda 0.30.4: xoroshiro128p_normal_float64 one-factor plain knock-out gives 1.35e7 paths/s (4x12) and 3.22e6 paths/s (8x52). Sample means 3.526 and 3.296 with sd 5.67 and 5.19 agree with P1's plain sigma. The CPU 16-process figures are 5.26e6 and 6.68e5 paths/s, so the anchor factor is about 2.6x (4x12) and 4.8x (8x52). The float64 exp+erfc pair rate is 1.06e9/s. The 1e-10 GPU/CPU agreement on identical points is achievable: libdevice and CPU transcendental functions differ by a few ULP, and Newton early-exit changes z by less than 1e-13(1+|z|).
fix: Replace the anchor bullet with: 'Plain-MC throughput anchor: numba.cuda xoroshiro128p_normal_float64 (create_xoroshiro128p_states, seed 2026100161), exact-date one-factor time stepping (common normal plus na idiosyncratic normals per date), plain knock-out payoff, 256-thread blocks, 8 blocks per SM. Paths per second at 4x12 and 8x52, median of 5 timed launches of at least 10 s each. The same construction on the 16 CPU processes gives the CPU anchor.'

section: C2 / C8 scope of timing runs
problem: 'Per (case, method)' does not say whether C2 covers only the knock-out or also the call and digital payoffs; including them roughly doubles C2. 'C2 (1 warm repeat)' in C8 does not say whether the repeat runs to 2^17 (C8's C1 depth) or to 2^19 (the C2 protocol). Both choices change the timing fit range behind the stop-rule T_C.
evidence: Spec C2 first bullet and C8 'C2 (1 warm repeat)'. The estimated C8 cost is about 45 min wall with C2 to 2^19, or about 22 min to 2^17.
fix: C2: 'Per development case and method in {rqmc, preint}, knock-out payoff only.' C8: 'C2 (1 warm repeat of 16 scrambles to 2^19; timing fit on marks 2^13..2^19).'
